subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Rates of change and compound measures

questions.q: Which formula correctly gives average speed?
questions.explain: Average speed is the total distance travelled divided by the total time taken.

questions.q: What is the correct formula for density?
questions.explain: Density is mass per unit volume, so density = mass ÷ volume.

questions.q: What is the correct formula for pressure?
questions.explain: Pressure is force per unit area, so pressure = force ÷ area.

questions.q: The ratio 12 : 18 written in its simplest form is:
questions.explain: Dividing both parts by the highest common factor 6 gives 2 : 3.

questions.q: If y is directly proportional to x, which equation represents the relationship (k is a constant)?
questions.explain: Direct proportion is written y = kx, where k is the constant of proportionality.

questions.q: If y is inversely proportional to x, which equation represents the relationship (k is a constant)?
questions.explain: Inverse proportion is written y = k/x, so the product xy stays constant.

questions.q: Which of these is a typical unit for density?
questions.explain: Density combines mass and volume units, for example g/cm³ or kg/m³.

questions.q: What does the graph of two quantities in direct proportion look like?
options: A straight line through the origin
A curve that never touches the axes
A straight line with a positive y-intercept
questions.explain: Direct proportion (y = kx) always gives a straight line passing through (0, 0).

questions.q: What does the graph of two quantities in inverse proportion look like?
options: A curve that approaches but never touches the axes
A straight line through the origin
questions.explain: Inverse proportion (y = k/x) produces a reciprocal curve that gets close to but never meets the axes.

questions.q: If y is inversely proportional to x, what happens to y when x is doubled?
questions.explain: In inverse proportion the product xy is constant, so doubling x halves y.

questions.q: If y is directly proportional to x, what happens to y when x is multiplied by 3?
questions.explain: In direct proportion y changes by the same factor as x, so tripling x triples y.

questions.q: The speed formula rearranged to make distance the subject gives:
questions.explain: Rearranging speed = distance ÷ time gives distance = speed × time.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1 : 50 000, what does 1 cm on the map represent?
questions.explain: A scale of 1 : 50 000 means each 1 cm on the map represents 50 000 cm (0.5 km) in reality.

questions.q: For a fixed distance, how are the speed of a journey and the time taken related?
questions.explain: With distance fixed, a higher speed means a shorter time, so speed and time are in inverse proportion.

questions.q: £60 is shared between two people in the ratio 2 : 3. How much does each person receive?
questions.explain: There are 5 parts, so one part is £12, giving 2 × £12 = £24 and 3 × £12 = £36.

questions.q: A car travels 150 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explain: Speed = distance ÷ time = 150 ÷ 2 = 75 km/h.

questions.q: An object has a mass of 60 g and a volume of 20 cm³. What is its density?
questions.explain: Density = mass ÷ volume = 60 ÷ 20 = 3 g/cm³.

questions.q: y is inversely proportional to x. When x = 3, y = 8. What is y when x = 6?
questions.explain: The constant k = xy = 3 × 8 = 24, so when x = 6, y = 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

questions.q: y is directly proportional to x. When x = 4, y = 12. What is y when x = 7?
questions.explain: The constant k = y ÷ x = 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so when x = 7, y = 3 × 7 = 21.

questions.q: Which of the following is a compound measure?
questions.explain: A compound measure combines two quantities; speed combines distance and time.
